teams.heading: Fiji's Wainiqolo relishing speed duel with France's Bielle-Biarrey in Lyon
teams.body: Fiji's Wainiqolo is relishing the prospect of facing Bielle-Biarrey, France's fellow speedster, in Lyon on Saturday. Fiji arrive after losing 39-24 to Wales in Cardiff and 73-8 to England, both in July, under coach Jake White, who was appointed after Senirusi Seruvakula's interim spell. Planet Rugby's preview expects France to use their attacking excellence to test a Fiji side it describes as having an underwhelming start to the Nations Championship.

lead.why: A new item about a named Fiji player's own pre-match outlook beats a preview column.

teams.heading: Fin Smith passes fitness test to start as Itoje returns for Australia
teams.body: Steve Borthwick has kept faith with the fly-half who was a doubt until late. Smith, who came off late in Northampton's defeat by Leicester on 24 October, has started England's past five Tests at 10 and is named in the run-on group. Itoje returns as captain, with Ben Curry making his Test return after an injury-hit 16 months. Greg Fisilau, uncapped, is on a forward-heavy bench.

lead.why: England's XV has just been named, and the headline change is Fin Smith passing his fitness test at fly-half.

teams.heading: Dupont and Ntamack reunite at half-back for first time since March 2025
teams.body: Planet Rugby's preview of Saturday's Lyon fixture describes it as a 20-month hiatus since the pair last started together at half-back. Ntamack has been hit by numerous injuries, including a long-running kidney problem, while Dupont missed the whole of July with a calf issue. Matthieu Jalibert is out with a quadriceps problem. Dupont captains the side, and Sarugbymag notes that locks Emmanuel Meafou and Thibaud Flament are among the absentees.

lead.why: It is the only NEW item about France's own selection, and it carries factual news (the Dupont-Ntamack half-back pairing), so it passes the opinion test that #4 otherwise would.

teams.heading: Jack Crowley injured, handing Sam Prendergast another shot at No. 10 against Argentina
teams.body: Farrell announced his team on Wednesday, and the number 10 berth is now open to Sam Prendergast while Crowley is sidelined by injury. Prendergast made his debut in this fixture two years ago, aged 21, and BBC Sport describes his Test career as uneven. Argentina have never beaten Ireland in Dublin, though they have won all three of their World Cup meetings. Ireland have won 14 of the 20 meetings between the sides.

lead.why: It is the newest Ireland selection story in the pack, covering the injury to Jack Crowley and the knock-on for the 10 jersey.

teams.heading: Ross Vintcent on Italy bench as cousin Riley Norton dropped by Springboks
teams.body: Ross Vintcent, the 24-year-old loose forward who qualifies for Italy through his maternal grandfather, had hoped to meet his second cousin in Saturday's Test in Turin, but Riley Norton was left out of Rassie Erasmus' match 23. Vintcent is named on the Azzurri bench. "Unfortunately, he wasn't selected, but they love watching Italy and me just as much as they love watching the Boks," Vintcent told Reuters. Vintcent has faced the Springboks three times without a win.

lead.why: It is a new Italy selection story with named players and a player quote, and it has a clear Azzurri angle.

teams.heading: Jack Dempsey names momentum as Scotland's first fix before All Blacks test
teams.body: Jack Dempsey will win his 36th Scotland cap against the All Blacks on Saturday. Scotland have had three near misses in a row under Gregor Townsend, and Dempsey puts the problem bluntly: "We can be the best team in the world for 20 minutes and we can be the worst team in the world for 20 minutes." His second point is messaging, which he says captain Sione Tuipulotu has been preaching, staying stronger together for longer. Habits will change, he says, if the moments keep stacking.

lead.why: A named player's direct on-record analysis of Scotland's core problem, broken by BBC Scotland with a fresh interview, and the strongest-scored new item about the team.

teams.heading: Bill Sweeney confirms WRU's formal approach to join Anglo-Welsh league
teams.body: Sweeney told BBC Radio Four the RFU has received a formal approach from the WRU asking to be part of an Anglo-Welsh tournament. The WRU has plans to cut one of its four professional sides, Ospreys, Cardiff, Scarlets or Dragons, which currently play in the 16-team United Rugby Championship. Sweeney said the English game remains the primary focus, and no formal talks have yet taken place with the Welsh side. The Prem hopes to grow from 10 to 12 teams for the 2029-30 season.

lead.why: A fresh, on-record RFU confirmation of a WRU approach that could reshape Welsh club rugby, and it is not a team-sheet or squad story already covered this week.

teams.heading: Bath sign Argentine prop Marcos Camerlinckx from Pampas XV
teams.body: Camerlinckx, 22, a former Argentina Under-20 international, has joined Bath. Director of rugby Johann van Graan told the club website: "We are looking forward to seeing how Marcos will develop his game over the next period of time and I am sure he will fit into our group very well." The tight-head arrives having won this year's Super Rugby Americas Championship with Pampas XV, and he played for an Argentina XV against the United States in August. Bath have not disclosed the length of his deal.

teams.heading: Wallabies name side for Twickenham, with Fraser McReight on 50th cap
teams.body: Fraser McReight will win his 50th cap at Twickenham, and Jeremy Williams starts at blindside flanker, forming a reshaped back row alongside captain Harry Wilson at number eight. Len Ikitau returns to midfield after missing the last Test under HIA protocols, pairing with Isaac Henry, who will make his first Test in the United Kingdom. Taniela Tupou is back on the bench, and Ryan Lonergan and Declan Meredith start in the halves.

lead.why: It is a new, concrete team announcement with a named milestone and a changed back row, and it is about Australia's own side.

teams.heading: Kingsley Jones, former Wales international, joins Japan camp this week before Cardiff
teams.body: Japan have a familiar face in the Cardiff build-up: Kingsley Jones, a former Wales international who left his role as Canada head coach last year, has spent four days in the camp. Eddie Jones says Kingsley Jones is "in camp, just watching what we're doing and feeding back on how we can improve." He was also involved in the camp before Japan's July 2025 win over Wales in Kitakyushu, and Japan are still seeking a first win on Welsh soil.

teams.heading: Jeremy Thrush and Sam McNicol join Hurricanes coaching staff for 2027
teams.body: The Hurricanes have completed their coaching group for the 2027 Super Rugby Pacific campaign, adding former All Blacks lock Thrush and former wing and centre McNicol as assistants. Thrush made 12 Test appearances for New Zealand and played 110 matches for the Hurricanes, one of 19 club centurions. McNicol, who made one Hurricanes appearance in 2015 before playing for the Chiefs, will also head the Hurricanes Hunters development side. “I’m extremely excited about connecting back up with the Hurricanes,” Thrush said.

lead.why: The only new item about New Zealand rugby itself, a confirmed staff announcement with named former All Blacks.

teams.heading: Erasmus recalls Moerat, starts Hooker on wing for injured Kolbe
teams.body: Salmaan Moerat is back from injury and starts in the second row, taking over from Eben Etzebeth, who is not in the side. Planet Rugby reports the rest of the selection is essentially the same team that beat the All Blacks in the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series. Kolbe is out injured, with Hooker named on the wing in his place. Italy coach Gonzalo Quesada says his side will be without several important, experienced players through injury.

lead.why: A new, concrete team selection with named changes (Moerat's return, Kolbe's injury, Hooker on the wing) that matters directly to the Springboks.
